scope: Read-only collection; no repo/Git changes or architecture decision.
findings: Eusebius VC IV.41–42 describes Tyre council and imperial letter; IV.43–47 describes separate Jerusalem dedication. Source is imperial panegyric.
Athanasius §§71–84 transmits partisan procedural complaints; §§77–79 are Egyptian bishops protests, §84 is the Jerusalem dedication/reception letter. Corrects initial delegated82–83 locator.
Eusebius narrates the Tyre council and then the Jerusalem dedication in tricennalia context (IV.40–47). They are separate events and locations; do not imply simultaneity or a precise interval.
No source consulted locates the council at a specific Tyrian building or on a beach. The title 'on the Shore' is not evidence for waterfront placement.

Tyre's ancient island/causeway/tombolo and harbors changed over time due to the Hellenistic causeway, sedimentation, harbor change and late Roman subsidence. Modern coast and archaeological property boundary are not a literal 335 shoreline.

chronologyGuardrail: Council and Jerusalem dedication are separate events; attribute narrative sequence to Eusebius, do not sharpen it into exact simultaneous timing.
geographyGuardrail: Tyre city-level location is supported; waterfront/building-specific venue unestablished. Modern coastlines, archaeological-park boundaries and medieval fabric are anachronistic controls for 335.
rights: UNESCO map pages showed no explicit open license; no map or image was copied.
